about: Does a broad 'how do I go about X' request select no skill, where the narrow form of the
same request selects one? Filed from plans/2026-09-01-broad-how-do-i-requests-select-no-skill.md,
which found python-refactor-audit's flagship case missing 5 of 6 live probes while three
narrower prompts for the same skill fired 3/3 on the same wording. Truncation and vocabulary
were both ruled out there, leaving the request's shape as the hypothesis.
One skill cannot answer that. These are three matched pairs, each targeting a different
high-usage skill, where the only difference within a pair is breadth: an open 'how do I go
about ...' against a specific question with the same subject. If the broad halves miss and the
narrow halves fire, the finding is about request shape and belongs in skill-fitness' guidance.
If only the original case misses, it is about that one description after all.
The two negatives are load-bearing here for an unusual reason: a broad prompt is exactly the
shape that could make a description fire on everything, so a suite of broad positives alone

cases.prompt: This module has grown for weeks and nobody has reviewed the whole thing. How do I go about cleaning up how its data is shaped?
Should this return a bare tuple or a NamedTuple?
I've got design work scattered across a bunch of repos. How do I go about keeping track of what's still open?
Create a plan file for this idea and set its status to idea.
I think agents keep ignoring my shell rules. How do I go about finding out whether that's actually true?
Measure how often my sessions pipe command output through head or tail.
What is the capital of France?
Rename this variable to something clearer.
